svg.title: Three shapes for work that takes longer than one function call should
svg.desc: Top row: the problem. One invocation that processes a whole file runs into three limits: an HTTP caller is cut off after 230 seconds, the function time-out stops the invocation, and a restart or scale-in loses everything that was in memory, so the work starts again from the beginning. Middle row, shape 1, accept then work: an HTTP or timer function accepts the request, puts a message on a queue and answers at once; a queue-triggered worker processes one bounded page and puts a continuation message on the queue for the next page until none is left; progress lives in the messages and in the data. Bottom row, shape 2, a durable orchestration: a client function starts an orchestration and returns 202 Accepted with a status URL; the orchestrator function calls activity functions one after the other, waits with durable timers and records every step in a history; after a restart the orchestrator is replayed from the history and continues with the next step; the caller polls the status URL and receives 202 while the run is in progress and 200 with the output when it is complete. A side note lists what each shape gives: the queue shape needs your own progress and status, the orchestration gives status, history, timers, retries and waiting for events.
svg.text: Long-running work: do not make one invocation longer, make the work resumable
The problem: one invocation does everything
read file → validate → 40 batches to Dataverse → report → move file
✗ HTTP caller is cut off after 230 seconds
✗ restart or scale-in: memory is gone
A throttled request means waiting inside a running (and billed) function.
After any interruption the work starts again from line 1, and nobody can ask "how far is it?".
Shape 1: accept, then work in bounded pieces (queue with continuation)
"all pages done" are yours to build
started · PrepareFeed done · chunk 0 done · chunk 1 done · timer 95 s …
after a restart the orchestrator is REPLAYED from here and continues
